name: Bosch Ltd.
business_summary: India-listed arm (70.5% held by Robert Bosch GmbH) of the global technology group. Mobility solutions (~85% of revenue, model knowledge): diesel and gasoline fuel-injection and powertrain systems, braking/ADAS electronics, two-wheeler and power-sports, and a large automotive aftermarket. Non-mobility: power tools, building technology, energy products. Net-cash, near debt-free; operating margin ~13-14%; sizeable treasury income. Q1 FY27 sales Rs 5,842 cr (+22% y/y), OPM 14%. Stock at a record high on 2026-11-04 (+76% since April) with first-ever bonus/split board meeting on 2026-11-06. P/E 64, price/book 10x.

new_nodes_proposed.name: Auto safety and emission norm tightening (ADAS/airbags, CAFE-III, BS-VII)

exposures.mechanism: Mobility ~85% of revenue (model knowledge; Q1 FY27 mobility +25.7% y/y per Autocar Professional); India share of mobility ~85% => +10% industry volumes ~ +8% revenue. Incremental margin ~25% vs 14% OPM => EBITDA +14%; EV/MCap ~0.95 (net cash); persistence 0.5 => ~+6.6. Stock already prices strong demand (P/E 64).

evidence.note: Q1 FY27 sales 5,842 cr (+22% y/y), OPM 14%

exposures.mechanism: Steel/forgings ~8% of costs (model knowledge) = ~7% of revenue; +7% => 0.5% of revenue; at 14% OPM => EBITDA -3.5%; ~50% passed through => -1.7%; x0.95 x persistence 0.3 => -0.5. Widened to -0.9 because pack shows empirical -1.34 per +10% global steel (t=-1.7, not significant).

Aluminium die-castings ~5% of costs => 4.3% of revenue; +10% => 0.43% of revenue => EBITDA -3.1%; 50% unrecovered => -1.5%; x0.95 x0.3 => -0.45. Aluminium is -19.6% since June, a current tailwind (reverse sign).
Copper (windings, sensors, harness) ~3% of costs => 2.6% of revenue; +10% => EBITDA -1.8%; 50% unrecovered => -0.9%; x0.95 x0.3 => -0.26.

Electronics/semiconductors are ~20% of mobility inputs (model knowledge). +1 (tightening, as in the 2025 Nexperia/chip disruption) => customer line stoppages and component shortage, ~-3% revenue; operating leverage 25% => EBITDA -5.4%; persistence 0.5 pushes down to ~-4.5 incl. expedite costs.

evidence.note: Bosch GmbH keeps outlook despite lower auto output

exposures.mechanism: Net importer: imported components/royalty-linked purchases ~20% of revenue vs exports ~6% (model knowledge) => net short ~14% of revenue; +3% => -0.4% of revenue => EBITDA -3%; 50% pass-through => -1.5%; x0.95 x0.5 => -0.7. Empirical -1.15 (t=-0.8) supports sign. INR already -6.5% over 12m.
P/E 64 and ROE ~15%: very long-duration equity. +25bp on cost of equity with (r-g)~4.5% => ~-2.5% on pure DCF, tempered by cash-rich balance sheet.

Higher repo raises vehicle-loan EMIs for CV/tractor/2W/PV buyers: ~-0.5% volumes per 25bp (assumption) => mobility revenue -0.4%; EBITDA -0.7%; x0.95x0.5 => -0.35. Discount-rate effect captured separately via G-sec to avoid double counting.

evidence.note: First hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening
Autocar Professional: rates + tough GST 2.0 base

exposures.mechanism: Diesel systems exposure: higher fuel cost lowers freight/trucking profitability and CV/tractor demand; pass-through to pumps limited. Empirical -0.26 (t=-0.5) is insignificant. +10% Brent => ~-0.5% via CV/diesel demand sentiment; low confidence.

Diesel/gasoline injection and ICE powertrain ~45-50% of mobility (model knowledge). +1 (a materially stronger EV push) lifts EV share ~5pp over 3 years => ICE content -5% on ~45% of revenue => -2.3% revenue, high-margin => EBITDA -6%; structural (persistence 1.0) but offset by content-per-EV and aftermarket => -3.

evidence.note: Automotive News: EV drain on Bosch

exposures.mechanism: Tighter safety (airbags/ESC/ADAS) and emission/CAFE norms raise content per vehicle for braking, sensors, gasoline direct injection and OBD, where Bosch has leading share. +1 step => ~+2% revenue on 3-year view at above-average margin => EBITDA +4%; x0.95 => ~+2.5 (analyst note, scanx 2026-11-04).
Premium mix in PV/2W lifts electronics, ABS/ESP and gasoline GDI content; Bosch 2W & power sports segment benefits. +1 => ~+1% revenue at above-average margin => +1.5.

Post-GST 2.0 (Sept 2025) the cuts lifted small-car and 2W demand; a further broad cut (+1) adds ~+3% auto volumes => mobility revenue +2.5%, EBITDA +4.4%; policy effects persist (1.0) but are shared across the industry and the 2025 cut is already in base => +2.
